subject: Civil Engineering
title: What Is Concrete?
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: What Is Concrete?.

hook.text: Concrete is the most used material on Earth after water. We pour 30 billion tons a year.

buildup.text: It's a mixture of cement, water, sand, and gravel — simple ingredients, remarkable strength.

discovery.text: Cement is the glue. When mixed with water, it hardens through a chemical reaction.

twist.text: Concrete is strong in compression but weak in tension — it cracks when pulled apart.

climax.text: That weakness led to reinforced concrete — steel handles tension, concrete handles compression.

punchline.text: Mix rocks, sand, cement, and water — and build civilization.

quiz.question: What is concrete's fundamental weakness?
options: It dissolves in water over time
It is strong in compression but weak in tension — it cracks under pulling forces
It cannot withstand temperatures above 100 degrees Fahrenheit

details.summary: Concrete is a composite material made by mixing cement, water, fine aggregate (sand), and coarse aggregate (gravel or crushed stone). When water reacts with cement in a process called hydration, it forms a hard matrix that binds the aggregates into the world's most widely used construction material.
details.whyItMatters: Concrete is the second most consumed substance on Earth after water. Understanding its composition is essential because almost every building, bridge, dam, and road depends on it.
takeaways: Concrete consists of cement paste binding sand and gravel aggregates together
Hydration, not drying, is the chemical reaction that hardens concrete
Over 14 billion cubic meters of concrete are produced globally each year

faq.question: What is the difference between cement and concrete?
faq.answer: Cement is a fine powder that acts as the binder, typically Portland cement made from limestone and clay. Concrete is the final product made by mixing cement with water, sand, and gravel. Cement typically makes up only 10 to 15% of concrete by volume.

faq.question: Why is concrete so much more popular than other building materials?
faq.answer: Concrete's ingredients are abundant and inexpensive worldwide. It can be cast into virtually any shape, hardens at room temperature, resists fire and water, and gains strength over decades. Its compressive strength rivals stone while costing a fraction of steel or timber per unit volume.
